title: Memoized fib, counted
prompt:
Implement `fib(n, memo, stats)` — recursive Fibonacci with explicit memoization:

- `memo` is a dict the function may read and write
- `stats` is a dict containing `'calls'`; increment `stats['calls'] += 1` at the top of EVERY invocation (including memo-hit returns)
- fib(0)=0, fib(1)=1, else fib(n-1)+fib(n-2)

The graded test calls `fib(25, {}, stats)` and asserts the value is 75025 and `stats['calls']` is under 60 (the never-reads-memo version makes ~243k calls).

tests.name: correct value, tiny call count
tests.code:
stats = {'calls': 0}
value = fib(25, {}, stats)
assert value == 75025, f'value: {value}'
assert stats['calls'] < 60, f'calls: {stats["calls"]} — memoization not effective'
print('ok')
tests.hint: Check the memo BEFORE recursing; increment stats at the very top of the function.
